body:
WHAT
OVERDRIVE is the fully-autonomous mode a user switches on with `/overdrive on`. While it is on, the permission engine lets every tool call run without asking: commands, network, file edits, deletions at any path, edits to `.magentra` state and `.env` files, and writes outside the workspace. The only thing that can still stop a call is a `deny` rule the user wrote in settings, and that refuses instead of asking.

WHY
An unattended run cannot answer a prompt; a single approval dialog would stall the whole task until the user comes back.

WHERE
engine/core/src/runtime/permissions.ts — PermissionEngine.check() (deny rules first via matches(this.deny, …); `!this.overdrive` guards on the protected-path branch, the deletionSubject computation and the out-of-workspace edit downgrade), PermissionEngine.setOverdrive(), private field `overdrive`, stanceDefault() returning "allow". Toggled from engine/core/src/runtime/session.ts — Session.setOverdrive() and engine/core/src/runtime/engine.ts — handleSlash() case "overdrive".

TEST CHECKLIST
1. With setOverdrive(true), check() for a Bash call whose deletionSubject returns a value resolves allowed:true with source "mode" and the requestApproval callback is never invoked.
2. With setOverdrive(true) and editProtectedPath set to a `.magentra/settings.json` path, check() allows without calling requestApproval.
3. With setOverdrive(true), a file-edit tool call with editOutsideWorkspace=true is allowed without a prompt (in normal mode the same call must call requestApproval with source "ask").
4. With setOverdrive(true) and a deny rule `Bash(rm *)`, check() for subject `rm -rf x` returns allowed:false, source "rule", and requestApproval is never invoked (it refuses, never asks).
5. With setOverdrive(true) and deletionScope "protected", a deletion of a `.magentra` directory still runs without a prompt.
